new.expl_en: To prevent changes to closed periods and keep reported numbers stable.

en: To stop changes to closed periods and keep reports stable
To make the software run faster at month end in practice as the work grows
To hide the transactions from auditors
To remove old customers from the system

new.stem_en: What does accounts payable represent?
new.expl_en: Money the company owes to suppliers.

en: Money the company owes to suppliers
Money that customers owe to the company
Money that is held in the bank account
Money paid to staff as salary

new.stem_en: What does a bank reconciliation compare?
new.expl_en: The company's cash book with the bank statement.

en: The cash book with the bank statement
The budget with the forecast for the business
The invoice with the original purchase request
The payroll with the tax return during the project

new.stem_en: Three-way matching compares which documents before paying a supplier?
new.expl_en: Purchase order, goods receipt and supplier invoice.

en: Purchase order, goods receipt and invoice
Quotation, contract and the payment slip in practice
Invoice, bank statement and the annual tax return
Budget, order and delivery schedule for the project

new.stem_en: An aged receivables report shows many invoices older than 90 days. What should the team do?
new.expl_en: Follow up on collections and assess the need for a provision for doubtful debts.

en: Follow up collections and assess a doubtful-debt provision
Delete the invoices from the ledger
Record them as revenue for the next year from the start in the long run
Offer a larger discount on new orders in a real project in many setups

new.stem_en: The bank statement shows a deposit of IDR 5 million that is not in the cash book. What is the correct treatment?
new.expl_en: Investigate and record it in the cash book (for example a customer transfer) so both agree.

en: Investigate it and record it in the cash book
Ignore it until the next audit
Reduce the bank balance in the books by the same amount
Record it as an expense of the month in a real project

new.stem_en: What is a budget?
new.expl_en: A plan of expected income and spending for a future period.

en: A plan of expected income and spending from the start for the project
A report of past income and spending
A list of the customers of the company and their orders
A record of the assets of the company

new.stem_en: What does a rolling forecast do?
new.expl_en: It is updated regularly and always looks a fixed number of periods ahead.

en: It is updated regularly and always looks ahead a fixed time
It is fixed once a year and rarely changed for the business in the long run
It records just what has already happened
It is written by the auditors

new.stem_en: What is the difference between CAPEX and OPEX?
new.expl_en: CAPEX buys long-term assets; OPEX covers day-to-day running costs.

en: CAPEX buys long-term assets, OPEX covers running costs within the team
CAPEX covers running costs, while OPEX buys long-term assets
CAPEX is for taxes, OPEX is for salaries
They are two names for the same cost

new.stem_en: A project costs IDR 100 million and returns IDR 40 million a year. What is the payback period?

en: 2.5 years
4 years
40 months
1.5 years

new.stem_en: In a DCF valuation, a higher discount rate does what to present value?
new.expl_en: It lowers the present value of future cash flows.

en: Lowers the present value
Raises the present value
Leaves it unchanged
Turns it negative in all cases

new.stem_en: What is the purpose of internal control?
new.expl_en: To safeguard assets, ensure reliable reporting and encourage compliance.

en: Safeguard assets and ensure reliable reporting
Increase the sales of the company
Reduce the number of employees
Replace the external audit

new.stem_en: What is segregation of duties?
new.expl_en: Splitting tasks such as authorising, recording and custody between different people.

en: Splitting authorising, recording and custody between people
Giving one person control of the whole process at that stage
Rotating staff between offices each year in practice within the team
Keeping each department in a separate building from the start

new.stem_en: Which is a preventive control?
new.expl_en: Approval limits that stop a payment before it is made.

en: An approval limit before a payment is made for the project
A monthly review of the bank statements by a manager
An audit after the year end
A report of last quarter's errors

new.stem_en: What is audit sampling?
new.expl_en: Testing a selected portion of items and drawing conclusions about the whole population.

en: Testing a selection and concluding about the whole population
Checking each single transaction of the year in many setups in many setups
Asking the management to pick the evidence
Reviewing just the largest customer

new.stem_en: An auditor finds that the same employee creates vendors and approves their payments. What is this?
new.expl_en: A segregation of duties weakness and a fraud risk.

en: A segregation-of-duties weakness and fraud risk
A normal efficiency in a small company at that stage
A strength of the purchasing process
A timing difference in the ledger

new.stem_en: Which cost stays the same regardless of production volume in the short run?
new.expl_en: A fixed cost, such as rent.

en: A fixed cost such as rent during the project
A variable cost such as raw materials in day-to-day work
A direct cost such as sales commission in most cases
A mixed cost such as electricity

new.stem_en: What does COGS stand for?
new.expl_en: Cost of goods sold (HPP).

en: Cost of goods sold
Cash on goods and services
Cost of general supplies
Capital of group subsidiaries

new.stem_en: Fixed costs are IDR 60 million, the selling price is IDR 50,000 and the variable cost is IDR 20,000 per unit. What is the break-even volume?

en: 2,000 units
1,200 units
3,000 units
1,500 units

new.stem_en: Purchases are 10 units at 100, then 10 units at 120. Under FIFO, what is the cost of the first 10 units sold?
new.expl_en: FIFO uses the oldest costs first: 10 x 100 = 1,000.

new.stem_en: Prices of materials are rising. Which inventory costing method reports the highest profit?
new.expl_en: FIFO expenses the oldest, lower costs first, so COGS is lower and profit higher when prices rise.

en: FIFO, which expenses the oldest costs first
Weighted average, which blends most the costs
Specific identification of each of the units that were sold
The method does not change the profit as the work grows
